title: Relative tensor cohomology of a module placed in an arbitrary degree
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $\Lambda$ a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], $R=\Lambda_X$ its pulled-back ring object [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and $C=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ the category of internal module objects in abelian sheaves [det-def-sfb-module-objects-sheaves]. Use its relative tensor [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor], unbounded derived category $D(C)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and Layer-B relative derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Use the direct-sum totalization and first-variable shift comparison $s^1_n$ of [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts] for the additive bifunctor $T=-\otimes_R-$. The comparison below is its $n=-q$ case, with first complex $S_0M$. For $M\in C$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$, let $S_qM$ be the cochain complex with $M$ in degree $q$, zero elsewhere, and zero differentials; write $M[0]$ for the image of $S_0M$ in $D(C)$. For $M,N\in C$ and $q,r\in\mathbf Z$, there are isomorphisms, natural in $M,N$,
$$
H^r\bigl(M[0][-q]\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N[0]\bigr)
\cong H^{r-q}\bigl(M[0]\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N[0]\bigr).
$$
More precisely, for every K-flat resolution $P\longrightarrow S_0N$ (a quasi-isomorphism with $P$ K-flat) [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso], the direct-sum total complex $\operatorname{Tot}(S_qM\otimes_R P)$ represents $M[0][-q]\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N[0]$. Its degree-$r$ term identifies with $M\otimes_R P^{r-q}$ and its differential with $(-1)^q(1_M\otimes d_P^{r-q})$. Under these identifications the identity maps give a chain isomorphism
$$
\operatorname{Tot}(S_qM\otimes_R P)
\cong \operatorname{Tot}(S_0M\otimes_R P)[-q].
$$
These comparisons commute with maps of $M$ and maps of K-flat resolutions, and their cohomology isomorphism above is independent of the chosen resolution under the canonical derived-tensor comparisons. There is no flatness assumption on $M,N$ and no restriction on the sign of $q,r$.
